study.trial_registration: University Hospital Medical Information Network (https://www.umin.ac.jp) ID 000028222
study.title: The Modifying of Functional Connectivity Induced by Peripheral Nerve Field Stimulation using Electroacupuncture for Migraine: A Prospective Clinical Study
study.population: Patients with migraine and age- and sex-balanced healthy controls
study.disease_condition: Migraine (migraine without aura [MWoA], migraine with aura [MWA], chronic migraine [CM])
study.inclusion_criteria: Patients 1) had migraine, 2) could be treated with acupuncture therapy once a week for 3 months, 3) had no history of other neurological disease, 4) had no other type of primary or secondary headache, 5) had been diagnosed with migraine more than 3 years previously, and 6) had no another acupuncture treatment during the study period
study.exclusion_criteria: 1) other type of headache (e.g., tension-type headache), 2) other neurological disorders (e.g., stroke, dementia, epilepsy) or malignancy, 3) migraine attack or headache during magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) examination, 4) claustrophobia, 5) pregnancy, and 6) prophylactic medications added or changed during the study period. For healthy controls: 1) history of migraine or other chronic headache and 2) hypertension, stroke, concussion, epilepsy, diabetes, or psychiatric disease

interventions.stimulation_type: Biphasic electrical pulse waves at 50 Hz applied subcutaneously in the bilateral occipital scalp region (C2 dermatome area)

interventions.manipulation_exact: Biphasic electrical pulse waves applied; intensity adjusted to just below the threshold of muscle contraction; needles not placed at any acupoints
interventions.electrical_intensity_exact: adjusted to just below the threshold of muscle contraction

interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: Stimulates the small branches of the nerve within the subcutaneous tissue of the C2 area innervated mainly by the greater occipital nerve

extraction_notes.note: Deqi and needle sensation were not measured or reported in this study. No deqi scale (e.g., MASS, Southampton Needle Sensation Questionnaire) was administered. This is noted in the methods and sensory_interoceptive_responses sections.

Expectancy, credibility, and blinding success were not formally assessed. Authors acknowledge that the study is open label without a sham electroacupuncture group and that placebo effects cannot be excluded.
The number of sessions is described as 'once a week for 3 months' but the exact total number of sessions is not explicitly stated (approximately 12–13 sessions depending on calendar).

Coordinate space (MNI or Talairach) for the hypothalamus ROI seed (X = –6, Y = –2, Z = –8) is not explicitly stated in the paper; coordinates are adopted from a previous study (Moulton et al. 2014). The coordinate space cannot be confirmed from this paper alone.

No MNI or Talairach coordinates are reported for the significant FC results; results are reported only as ROI-to-ROI edge-level statistics without spatial coordinates for the regions. The 13 ROI locations (other than the hypothalamus seed) are not given with coordinates.

The T-value sign convention in Table 3 is described as 'FC of positive T values showed a significant decrease after acupuncture,' which is slightly counterintuitive. The extracted T(10) = 4.06 is preserved as reported. The direction (decrease in FC post-acupuncture) is explicitly stated in both the table note and narrative.

The T-value signs in Table 4 for MWoA > CM are listed as negative values (e.g., –2.72, –3.52, –3.12, –3.59) under the heading 'MWoA > CM'. This appears to reflect the direction of the t-test contrast (CM subtracted from MWoA), such that negative T indicates CM < MWoA. Preserved as reported.

The n_analyzed for the MWoA vs CM comparison (Table 4, MWoA > CM) is listed as T(15), implying degrees of freedom = 15, which is consistent with n=11 (MWoA) + n=6 (CM) – 2 = 15. Similarly T(27) for CM vs control implies 29 participants. These are preserved as reported.
The total n_total_enrolled is inferred as 50 (26 migraine + 24 healthy controls as stated in the abstract and methods). This is consistent with the paper text.
The MWA group (n=3) was excluded from FC analysis due to small sample size, as stated in the methods. Clinical outcomes for MWA are not reported separately in Table 2.
The paper does not report the electrical stimulator output units for intensity (only 'just below the threshold of muscle contraction'), so numeric intensity cannot be extracted.

The paper does not describe the OhmPulser LFP-4000A stimulator parameters beyond frequency (50 Hz), waveform (biphasic), and duration (15 minutes). Pulse width, current amplitude ranges, and other parameters are not reported.
The paper does not report data availability, data sharing, or supplementary materials.
Figure 4 shows the FC change result but coordinates cannot be read from the figure. The result is captured via Table 3 which provides sufficient statistics.
Motion exclusion criteria for fMRI preprocessing are not explicitly stated beyond 'head motion correction'; no maximum displacement or rotation thresholds are reported.
Band-pass filtering parameters for the rsfMRI signal are not reported.
